name: 1010music Bento
note: Audio ports from its manual: until it's read, the rig draws only its MIDI and guesses no port.

ports.label: MIDI IN
ports.about: MIDI into the Bento: clock, Start and Stop when the tape leads.

ports.label: MIDI OUT
ports.about: MIDI from the Bento: its notes, and its clock when it sets the tempo.

hardware.extending: Not on the Pi's USB today: it feeds the Sidekick, and a KeyStep 37 is plugged into the Bento's USB host port. Its ports above are still the placeholder's MIDI pair; the audio and USB ports wait on its manual (firmware v1.2). If it is ever plugged into the Pi, capture its ids from the device port, and settle how the tape's clock should reach it. Everything under "hardware" is ignored by the Go loader: it is notes for people, and for a later registry (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-device-profiles-design.md). To fill this profile from a real unit, follow 'Capturing an unknown device' in docs/hardware/README.md, then flip statuses from 'unconfirmed' or 'to-capture' to 'owner'.

connection.note: Audio goes into the Sidekick (jack 2 on the current patch). No USB link to the Pi as of Oct 2026. It has no speaker, which makes casual jamming awkward.

audio.outputs: three stereo, plus one stereo headphone
audio.recording: WAV to microSD, up to 4 hours; long WAVs stream from the card

midi.usb: host and device ports both carry MIDI
midi.trs: two inputs and two outputs, Type A and Type B, with a Type B TRS to 5-pin DIN adapter in the box

current_use.note: A KeyStep 37 is connected to its USB host port over USB MIDI.

storage.card: microSD, included; projects, samples and recordings live on it

controls.$comment: Not read from the manual here. Before drawing a labelled diagram, take the control layout from the user manual (firmware v1.2, Oct 2025).

quirks.text: Two USB-C ports: one host, one device, both supporting audio and MIDI.
Needs a 30 W USB supply providing at least 2000 mA at 5 V; the supply is not included.
The product page gives two different counts for the factory content on the card (about 160 patches and 200 WAV files; 155 patches and over 5000 sample files).

unknowns.question: Vendor and product ids on the device port
unknowns.how: If connected to the Pi: lsusb before and after plugging in

unknowns.question: How should the tape's MIDI clock reach it, given it is not on the Pi's USB?
unknowns.how: Decide between USB device port to the Pi and a TRS MIDI out from the Pi; test the one chosen with the tape's clock running

unknowns.question: Does it respond to program change to pick patterns?
unknowns.how: Check the v1.2 manual's MIDI section, then send a program change and watch

hindsight.role: Groovebox and arranging surface for melodic and multitrack parts. Notes are made on it; Hindsight catches the audio.
notes: The tape is meant to lead the clock and the Bento to follow.
